events.what: Aires and Kahn prove asymptotic lower bounds on the balance constant delta(P) for posets of large width (delta(P) -> 1/2 under width/minimal-element conditions; delta(P) >= 1/e - o(1) under weaker width conditions)
Aires and Kahn study variance vs. range for linear extensions and balancing extensions in posets of bounded width
Gupta's exhaustive census verifies the Gold Partition Conjecture (hence 1/3-2/3) for all posets on at most 14 elements
events.ai_basis: Anthropic Claude Code (Claude 5 family) and OpenAI Codex (GPT-5.6 family) were used extensively for software development and optimization, computational experiment design, literature discovery, and drafting and editing the manuscript.

judgement.doubts: Agree with the 2026-09-24 hand corrections. Gupta's census is instances (F4) and is discarded; its AI disclosure (software, experiment design, literature, prose) would be none anyway, since no mathematics in the result is attributed to the models. Possible upgrade to partial: if the Aires-Kahn asymptotics (delta -> 1/2, or >= 1/e - o(1) > 1/3) imply the conjecture for all sufficiently large posets in a width-defined class, that is a case settlement. The record describes the hypotheses only loosely ('width/minimal-element conditions') and the o(1) terms are ineffective, so I keep bound. Aires-Kahn acknowledgements were not read in full.

corrections.why: F3: kept as progress, with doubt. The record says Aires-Kahn give delta(P) -> 1/2 and delta(P) >= 1/e - o(1) (with 1/e > 1/3) under width conditions. That could settle the conjecture for large enough posets of a restricted class, which would be a case (partial). The record states the hypotheses too vaguely to confirm that, so the bound reading stands.
